page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-64 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture features 2 threads per core with dedicated vCPU allocation, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Advanced instruction sets include AVX-512 (supporting F, VNNI, and BF16 extensions), AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and VAES. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a generous 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation highlights exceptional single-threaded performance alongside balanced multi-threaded compute capability. Single-core tests place the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2666.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 3462.99, and single-threaded gzip compression at 38.34 GB/sec. Multi-core performance aligns with expected eight-thread capacity, posting an average-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 10508.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 17732.98. Memory subsystems demonstrate strong throughput with a PassMark memory score of 2785.17 and uncached read bandwidth reaching 52.48 GB/sec.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides favorable cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise tasks that do not require extensive parallel core scaling. Because persistent local disks are absent, stateful architectures must rely on network-attached storage volumes. VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-64 is well suited for in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-64 provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 vector acceleration and hardware encryption extensions, the instance supplies 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, requiring external network-attached storage for persistence. In performance testing, the instance exhibits top-tier single-core metrics, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2666.0 and 38.34 GB/sec single-threaded gzip compression, while multi-core compute and PassMark CPU metrics maintain reliable median performance. With its high memory-per-core density and solid memory throughput, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads including Redis caches, relational databases, backend microservices, and general business applications.
